summary.title: Lost in Stories: Consistency Bugs in Long Story Generation by LLMs

details: LLMs can now write tens of thousands of words but contradict their own established facts, character traits, and world rules; existing long-form/story benchmarks score plot quality and fluency rather than systematically detecting cross-context contradictions.

ConStory-Bench: a benchmark of 2,000 long-story generation prompts (four task scenarios: generation, continuation, expansion, completion; target 8,000-10,000 words) paired with a consistency-error taxonomy of 5 categories and 19 fine-grained subtypes (timeline/plot logic, characterization, world-building, factual detail, narrative style).

ConStory-Checker: an LLM-as-judge pipeline that extracts contradiction-prone spans per category, pairs them into consistent/contradictory verdicts, and grounds every judgment in an evidence chain of exact quotations with character-level offsets emitted as structured JSON.

Score consistency with two complementary length- and difficulty-aware metrics: Consistency Error Density (errors per 10K words) and Group Relative Rank (within-prompt ranking of a length-aware quality score words/(1+errors)).
Seed stories/queries drawn from seven public corpora (LongBench, LongBench-Write, LongLamp, TellMeAStory/Storium, WritingBench, WritingPrompts, WikiPlots).

o4-mini rewrites each seed into a task-typed prompt with an 8K-10K word target; MinHash deduplication plus manual/heuristic filtering yields 2,000 prompts (751 generation, 432 continuation, 422 expansion, 395 completion).
o4-mini also serves as the judge model in the four-stage ConStory-Checker pipeline.
Proprietary: GPT-5-Reasoning, Gemini-2.5-Pro/Flash, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, Grok-4, GPT-4o, Doubao-1.6-Thinking, Mistral-Medium-3.1.
Open-source: Qwen3 family (4B to 235B-A22B-Thinking), GLM-4.5/4.6, DeepSeek-V3/R1/V3.2-Exp, Kimi-K2, Ring-1T, Ling-1T, Step3, MiniMax-M1, etc.

Capability-enhanced long-writing models (LongWriter-Zero, Suri-i-ORPO, LongAlign-13B) and agentic pipelines (SuperWriter, DOME); each system runs all 2,000 prompts under a shared storyteller system prompt.
Diagnostic set: 200 stories generated by Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking with 1,000 deliberately injected errors spanning all five categories (200 per category).
Two professional web-novel writers independently annotated the same stories (paid $1.00/story) following the taxonomy; injected errors are ground truth for precision/recall/F1.
Length dynamics: output-length distributions per model plus per-length-bin average error counts and length-error Pearson correlations.

Uncertainty: token-level Shannon entropy (plus probability and perplexity) of error segments vs whole-text baseline for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, decoding at temperature 0.7, top-k 20, top-p 0.95.
Co-occurrence: pairwise Pearson correlations among the five error categories; positional analysis records normalized fact position, contradiction position, and their gap per error subtype.

key_findings.finding: Most current LLMs still fail at long-form narrative consistency, with factual/detail and timeline errors as the dominant failure modes and one clear frontier leader.
key_findings.evidence: GPT-5-Reasoning attains the lowest overall CED (0.113 errors per 10K words) and best GRR (3.05), ahead of Gemini-2.5-Pro (0.305) and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 (0.520); weaker systems reach 3.4-3.7 CED (MiniMax-M1-80k 3.447, LongAlign-13B 3.664). Category CEDs are consistently highest for Factual & Detail and Timeline & Plot Logic; open-ended Generation prompts yield the highest CED for most models.

key_findings.finding: The automated evidence-grounded checker detects narrative contradictions far more reliably than paid professional human annotators.
key_findings.evidence: On the 1,000 injected-error diagnostic set, ConStory-Checker achieves precision 0.884, recall 0.550, F1 0.678 versus human experts' 0.660/0.139/0.229; it finds 550 errors vs 138.5 average human true positives (about 3.2x higher discovery rate), with per-category F1 up to 0.742 (characterization).

key_findings.finding: Consistency errors occur where the model is locally uncertain, making token-level entropy an early-warning signal.
key_findings.evidence: Error-bearing segments show higher mean entropy than whole-text baselines: +19.24% for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (1.2799 vs 1.0734) and +12.03% for Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (1.2814 vs 1.1438); probability drops (-7.99%/-5.41%) and perplexity rises (+5.55%/+2.54%) in the same segments.

key_findings.finding: Errors are positionally structured rather than uniform: contradictions cluster in the middle of narratives and fact-to-contradiction gaps vary systematically by error type.
key_findings.evidence: Averaged over models, facts are established at 14-24% of story length while contradictions appear at 34-49%; geographical contradictions have the largest gap (31.0%) and absolute-time contradictions 29.7%, whereas perspective confusions have a gap of only 4.7% (fact 13.7%, contradiction 12.2%), indicating local rather than long-range failure.

key_findings.finding: Error categories cluster along dependency chains centered on factual detail, while stylistic errors are mechanistically independent.
key_findings.evidence: Pooled Pearson correlations show Factual & Detail as a hub, correlating with Characterization (r=0.304), World-building (r=0.255), and Timeline (r=0.176), while Narrative & Style has near-zero correlations with all others; model-specific matrices reach r=0.533-0.556 for Char.-Fact. in GLM-4.6 and Kimi-K2-2509.
